question: What directional relationship do yellow center line markings and white lane line markings communicate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Yellow center line markings communicate that traffic on either side of the line is traveling in opposite directions, while white lane line markings communicate that the lanes they separate carry traffic in the same direction. In short, yellow = opposing flows; white = same-direction flows. The pattern of the yellow line (broken vs. solid) further communicates whether passing across the line is permitted. Standards (mandatory): - "Center line pavement markings, when used, shall be the pavement markings used to delineate the separation of traffic lanes that have opposite directions of travel on a roadway and shall be yellow." - "When used, lane line pavement markings delineating the separation of traffic lanes that have the same direction of travel shall be white." - On two-lane, two-way roadways, "The center line markings on two-lane, two-way roadways shall be one of the following as shown in Figure 3B-1: A. Two-direction passing zone markings consisting of a normal width broken yellow line where crossing the center line markings for passing with care is permitted for traffic traveling in either direction; B. One-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of a double yellow line, one of which is a normal width broken yellow line and the other is a normal width solid yellow line, where crossing the center line markings for passing with care is permitted for the traffic traveling adjacent to the broken line, but is prohibited for traffic traveling adjacent to the solid line; or C. Two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of two normal width solid yellow lines where crossing the center line markings for passing is prohibited for traffic traveling in either direction." - "Except where a reversible lane (see Section 3B.04) or a two-way left-turn lane (see Section 3B.05) is present, the center line markings on undivided two-way roadways with four or more lanes for moving motor vehicle traffic always available shall be the two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of normal width double solid yellow lines as shown in Figure 3B-2." Options (permitted): - Solid white lane line markings may be used: on approaches to intersections to separate contiguous through lanes; to separate through traffic lanes from auxiliary lanes, such as an added uphill truck lane; and on approaches to crosswalks across multi-lane roadways. - On shared-use paths wide enough for two minimum-width lanes, a solid yellow center line may be used to separate the two directions of travel where passing or traveling to the left of the line is not permitted, and a broken yellow center line may be used where passing is permitted. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3B-2 shows multi-lane, two-way roadways where the double solid yellow line separates opposing directions (arrows pointing opposite ways on either side of the yellow line) while broken white lane lines separate same-direction lanes. [Image 2] Figure 3B-3 shows three-lane, two-way applications where the yellow center line (broken-and-solid or double solid) divides opposing flows and a white lane line divides the two same-direction lanes. [Image 3] Figure 3B-1 shows two-lane, two-way markings with broken and solid yellow center line combinations indicating where passing is permitted or prohibited between the opposing directions. [Image 4] The page 582 figure repeats the Figure 3B-2 multi-lane layouts, with yellow separating opposing arrows and white lines within each direction. [Image 5] The page 583 figure repeats Figure 3B-3, showing yellow between opposing flows and white between the two same-direction lanes. [Image 6] The page 595 lane-drop figure shows white lane lines (including wide dotted and channelizing lines) used exclusively between same-direction freeway lanes, with yellow only on the left edge. [Image 7] The page 674 crosswalk figure shows a double yellow center line between opposing traffic arrows and white lane lines between same-direction lanes, each supplemented by tubular markers. gold_answer: Yellow center lines separate lanes traveling in opposite directions. White lane lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction.
